messages:
deploy-bot: initiating canary rollout v2.16.0 -> auth-service (us-west-2 / us-east-1). Canary set to 7% across weighted regions. New secret reference: AUTH_KMS_KEY_ID=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/new-rotated-2026 (parameterized via config-service).

deploy-bot: Canary successful in creating pods, routing traffic. Observability hooks live.

rachel: noticing immediate uptick in auth latencies and some 401s in us-west-2 canary pods. Traces point to decrypt errors.

ivy: sample error from pod-xyz: ```ERROR: KMS.Decrypt AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789:assumed-role/redwood-node-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/new-rotated-2026```

oncall-jay: paging oncall. incident-bot page SRE. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Paging @oncall-jay (oncall). P1: auth-service canary decrypt/access failures in us-west-2.

oncall-jay: here. pulling logs. are both regions affected?

tom: looks localized to us-west-2 canary instances. us-east-1 uses alias that still points to old key. Mixed behavior because config-service updated different region shards at different times.

eng-olga: quick investigation: new key's grants only include the redeployed node-role (arn:...:role/redwood-node-role-prod). Our canary pods assume a different role due to old instance profile naming on canary machines (arn:...:role/redwood-node-role-canary). policy lacks that principal.

ops-max: checking CloudTrail -> many kms:Decrypt entries for new-rotated-2026 show AccessDenied for assumed-role redwood-node-role-canary. The old key has Allow for both roles. The rotation script replaced key id but didn't propagate expected grants to the canary role.

pm-lee: immediate mitigation: what can we flip fast? options: revert config change so pods use old key, flip runtime flag to route canary away from new key, or patch key policy to include canary role. Fastest user-facing is stop canary traffic to affected pods. I can toggle the rollout gate.

pm-lee: stopping canary ramp and freezing rollout now. Pausing traffic to canary instances in us-west-2.

rachel: after pause, error rate falls back to baseline for majority of requests. Some sessions that hit canary still show 401s while draining.

incident-bot: Mitigation applied by pm-lee: canary traffic freeze and rollback hold. Please verify.

oncall-jay: containment achieved. next: decide whether to patch KMS policy or to roll back config-service change. Which is auditable?

eng-olga: prefer patching key policy to add the canary principal (short term) then fix rotation job so grants are applied atomically for all target principals. Rolling back config may be disruptive across regions.

ops-max: preparing policy patch. Draft diff below: ```- "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-node-role-prod"}, + "Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-node-role-prod","arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-node-role-canary"]}```

oncall-jay: to be safe, hold on applying until we have approvers listed and we run a decrypt smoke test. eng-olga and ops-max, please post the smoke command you will run.

ops-max: will run: ```aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://auth_token.enc --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/new-rotated-2026 --region us-west-2``` and confirm EC2 role mapping in cloudtrail.

eng-olga: approved by eng-olga. applying patch in 30s.

ops-max: policy applied. running decrypt test from a canary instance via SSM session: result -> success. CloudTrail shows Decrypt allowed for redwood-node-role-canary.

rachel: after policy apply and re-route, canary pods no longer show AccessDenied. Latency returning to baseline.

pm-lee: re-enabling canary ramp to 2% for 5 minutes, then 7% if stable. Abort if decrypt errors >0.2% or 5xx increase >1%.

deploy-bot: canary ramp: 2% -> hold.

eng-olga: also added temporary synthetic decrypt check to the canary health probe. If decrypt fails, the pod will be marked unhealthy and removed.

tom: observing metrics: decrypt error count = 0 for last 6m, auth latency stable. Proceed with ramp.

pm-lee: ramping to 7% now. monitoring closely.

incident-bot: Remediation: canary freeze, KMS policy update to include canary principal, added decrypt probe. Status: contained -> recovering.

noncall-jay: impact summary: roughly 700 auth failures over a 9-minute window affecting ~5% of sessions (canary users in us-west-2). No token compromise. Customer-facing auth loss limited and brief.

eng-olga: immediate follow-ups: 1) patch rotation job to apply grants for both prod & canary principals; 2) add post-rotation validate step performing decrypt with representative principals; 3) update deploy pipeline to include region-shard config parity checks before rollout; 4) codify key-grant checklist in runbook. Assign owners: ops-max -> key rotation automation; eng-olga -> decrypt-smoke tests; rachel -> dashboard alert tuning; pm-lee -> customer comms and postmortem.

pm-lee: drafted customer note: "A small percentage of authentication requests experienced failures during a canary deployment due to a KMS key rotation grant omission. We paused the rollout, applied a fix, and resumed. We will publish a full postmortem and remediation plan." Sending to support after PM review.

ops-max: uploading CloudTrail extracts and key-policy diffs to incident ticket.

oncall-jay: handing off oncall to tom for remainder of shift. tom: you ok to take?

tom: taking handoff. monitoring for 30 more min then will close.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by oncall-jay. Please attach postmortem for archiving.

eng-olga: opened PR to change rotation job and added tests. ops-max will add an automated check to fail rotations that do not include required principals.

rachel: closing alert rules and adding split metrics to surface cross-region alias mismatches earlier.

pm-lee: postmortem owner assigned. ETA 48 hours. Will coordinate customer follow-up.

ops-max: final note: rotate-and-verify pattern now required for any key alias updates; tagging infra team for compliance.

oncall-jay: final timeline: config-service updated key -> canary started -> decrypt AccessDenied observed -> canary freeze -> KMS policy patch -> decrypt tests pass -> canary resumed -> stable. Impact: brief auth failures for subset of canary users.

pm-lee: closing channel handoff. thanks all. :pray:
